Risk scenario: Credential theft or reuse could allow unauthorized access
Proposed treatment: Confirm important services and supported MFA requirements
Priority basis: First follow-up because authentication gaps may affect access to important services; service scope and business impact require confirmation

Risk scenario: Unnecessary access could persist after role changes or departures
Proposed treatment: Document approvals and revocation; examine authorized samples
Priority basis: Assess after services and owners are scoped so access approvals and revocation can be traced against defined records

Risk scenario: Unclear roles and procedures could delay incident response
Proposed treatment: Define contacts and reporting; develop practical response guidance
Priority basis: Assign responsibility early because unclear ownership and reporting can delay triage and escalation

Risk scenario: Inconsistent awareness could enable phishing or delay reporting
Priority basis: Address after workforce roles are scoped; training and reporting instructions are foundational follow-up for the reported awareness gap

Risk scenario: Untracked technology could miss updates or access removal
Priority basis: Inventory is a prerequisite for scoping access

Risk scenario: An unverified backup may not support restoration when needed
Proposed treatment: Gather backup evidence; plan authorized recovery validation
Priority basis: Confirm backup scope and restoration evidence; no backup failure was demonstrated in the source report

Risk scenario: Untracked service dependencies could leave responsibilities unclear
Proposed treatment: Inventory providers and review relevant agreements
Priority basis: Confirm provider inventory before contract review because agreement existence does not establish supplier coverage
